name: Julia E. Miller
title: El Camino Healthcare District Board Secretary/Treasurer
years_of_service: First elected to the District Board in November 2012; re-elected in November 2016, November 2020, and November 2024. Current term expires November 2028. Per the District's own Board of Directors biography page, she is one of the Board's two longest-serving Directors alongside Board Chair John Zoglin (service since 2007).
background: Miller is retired from Lockheed Martin and formerly served as Mayor and a Council member for the City of Sunnyvale for eight years, before her 2012 election to the El Camino Healthcare District Board, where she is now Board Secretary/Treasurer. She is also an owner of Miller Enterprises, represents the District as vice president of the Silicon Valley Tobacco Securitization Authority Board, has served as vice-chair of the Association of California Healthcare Districts Board, and has served on the Bay Area Air Quality Management District and San Francisco Bay Trail boards, per the District's own Board of Directors biography page. She resides in Sunnyvale.

As Board Secretary/Treasurer, Miller moved adoption of Resolution No. 2026-06 on May 19, 2026, placing Measure S on the November 3, 2026 ballot; the resolution passed 3-2 (Miller, Fung, and Somersille in favor; Chair Zoglin and Director Ting opposed), seconded by Dr. Somersille. Measure S would cap a District Director's service at four full four-year terms (16 years) going forward, but the cap does not count any term served before December 1, 2026, meaning it resets to zero for every sitting Director, including Miller, who by that reset would not be constrained until years from now despite already having served four elected terms. Miller drafted the official Argument in Favor together with the District's Chief Legal Officer and signed it on the Board's behalf after the Board voted 4-1 (Zoglin again the lone no vote) on June 23, 2026 to approve it for the county's Voter Information Guide. Full detail on the measure, including the legal constraints under Government Code Section 53077 that shaped its design, is covered in content/measures/scc-measure-s-2026.json and not duplicated here.

This profile's sourcing on Miller's District tenure and role comes from the District's own Board of Directors biography page and from the measure file's sourcing of Board packet materials and meeting minutes; WebSearch was unavailable (session budget exhausted) and no independent news coverage of Miller specifically, beyond the Measure S reporting already cited in the measure file, was located in this session. Her specific votes on other District matters, beyond the Measure S resolution and argument votes, were not reviewed.
attendance: No individually published Director-by-Director meeting-attendance or voting-participation scorecard for the El Camino Healthcare District Board was found in this session. The District publishes full Board meeting packets, including agendas and draft minutes (as cited in content/measures/scc-measure-s-2026.json for the May 19, 2026 and June 23, 2026 meetings), which record individual votes on specific agenda items and would in principle allow a manual tally, but compiling a comprehensive attendance record across meetings was not feasible within this session's tool budget.
